_comment: Which column holds the address. Read by BOTH detectors:
The file exists because the panel and the server disagreed for a day.
On 2026-09-02 the panel started accepting 'Email Address' and the server
kept demanding a header spelled exactly 'email', so the newly accepted
file was refused later and worse: after the campaign row existed, with an
English sentence no locale translates, leaving a 0-recipient campaign in
Reports. render_cases.json exists for the same reason on the body side.
A case added here must pass on both sides or neither. That is the point:
there is no way to fix one detector and forget the other.

cases.why: the plain case that already worked — it must keep working
what an ATS or CRM export writes, and what turned Dhirender away twice
hyphenated, and not the first column
underscored
shouting, with a space
Turkish header — no name list would have had this
Chinese header, found from the data
Arabic header, found from the data
no email column at all — this must still be refused
one stray address in a notes field is not an email column
named correctly but empty — the name pass answers before the data does
hyphenated AND empty — only header normalisation can find this
the ATS spelling with no data to fall back on
one address in four is a notes field, not an email column
two rows is not enough to name a column from its contents
three is — the row above and this one are the boundary
a padded header the name list knows — answered before the data is read
padded AND unlisted, so only the content pass can answer. The server keys rows by the header AS WRITTEN, so sampling by the trimmed name reads back nothing and this is the only case that catches it
the exact shape of the file in the 0.3.3 review: accepted by the panel, 400'd by the server
a plainly-named 'email' column outranks any alias, wherever it sits. First-match sent this campaign to the private addresses — a wrong send, and mail cannot be recalled
same rule when the alias is first: the person, not reception
'Mail' as a postal or yes/no column. First-match picked it, every row came out invalid, and the user got a campaign with no recipients from a file that worked the day before
